feature: In-pattern variable reuse — one name at two node positions of ONE pattern is a JOIN, not a rebind

scenarios.name: a reused name on a single hop asks for a self-loop and returns only the self-looped node
scenarios.note: The cycles fixture is the discriminating one: A->B->C->A plus S->S. `(a)-[:PG_LINKS]->(a)` asks for an edge whose two endpoints are the same entity, which ONLY S satisfies. Before req-grid-traversal-lang-shape-9 the repeat position contributed no binding and therefore no constraint, so the same query returned every node and every edge in the fixture (tap#743) — the answer this scenario's expected envelope is shaped to reject. Do not 'simplify' the fixture to one without a self-loop: the case would then be empty-over-empty and prove nothing.

scenarios.name: a two-hop walk closing on its origin returns only the node that can close in two hops
scenarios.note: The three-node cycle needs THREE hops to return to A, so a two-hop closed walk excludes A, B and C and admits only the self-looped S (S->S->S). Unfixed, the closing `(a)` was tied to nothing and the query returned all four nodes and all four edges — a superset the size of the second position's fan-out. The gap between 'all four' and 'one' is the whole assertion.
scenarios.inspired_by: opencypher TCK — clauses/match (cyclic path returns to origin)

scenarios.name: a three-hop walk closing on its origin admits the three-node cycle and the self-loop
scenarios.note: The positive companion to the two-hop case: at three hops the A->B->C->A cycle DOES close, so the unification must ADMIT it rather than merely exclude things — a scenario that only ever shrinks a result set cannot tell a correct join from a filter that rejects everything. S->S->S->S closes too, which is why the self-loop is in the expected envelope alongside the cycle. HONEST LIMIT, measured: on THIS fixture the unfixed engine returns the same four nodes (every length-3 walk starts somewhere in the cycle), so this case discriminates on the SQL SNAPSHOT — the missing `T7.to_entity_id = tap_edge.from_entity_id` closure — and not on the envelope. The envelope discrimination lives in the self-loop and two-hop cases, which go from one node to all four when the unification is removed. Keep all three.
scenarios.inspired_by: opencypher TCK — clauses/match (cyclic path returns to origin)

scenarios.name: one name used for both a node and an edge position is refused with the remedy named
scenarios.note: The reuse shape that is NOT a join: a node binds an Entity and an edge binds an Edge row, so no value can be both. Under the old first-occurrence-wins binding this silently aliased — accepted, and answering a different question. The refusal is part of the contract, which is why it is pinned here and not left to the effect suite alone.
scenarios.inspired_by: opencypher TCK — no applicable feature folder (TAP-native: the TCK has no node/relationship name-collision rejection case)

expected_error.message_contains: names both a node and an edge
